newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mostly lower.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed mostly lower on Friday as long-liquidation by local investors erased earlier price gains, traders said.
The spot November contract ended up 60 yen at 17,510 yen a tonne. Others were 60 to 250 yen lower, and the benchmark September contract was down 250 yen at 16,900.

A stronger Chicago market encouraged local investors to buy from the opening, the traders said. But individual investors, who hold many long positions in nearby months, actively sold by afternoon, they said.
The Tokyo corn futures market will be closed next Monday due to a national holiday. Trading will be resumed on Tuesday.
The CBOT corn and soybean prices on Project A overnight trading system were lower during Tokyo afternoon.
The December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.29 per bushel at 0825 GMT, against $3.30 at Thursday's close.
The November contract of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $8.14 at 0825 GMT, against $8.14-1/2 from Thursday's close.
